Directed by Silvio Soldini

Pane e Tulipani

Presented by Mediterranean Foods

An international hit 25 years ago, director Silvio Soldini’s gently subversive comedy of womanhood and middle age is delightful, quirky and utterly charming. It’s the story of Rosalba, a mother and housewife who is so taken for granted, that her family leave her behind, forgetting her at a rest stop on a tour bus holiday.

Instead of going home, Rosealba defiantly sets out on a life-changing adventure to Venice.

The cast of eccentric and colourful characters she meets along the way is led by the wonderfully deadpan Bruno Ganz as Fernando, the Icelandic waiter. But back home her overbearing husband Fermo, hires a plumber to track her down in Venice.

Each character has their own poetic eccentricity, populating the film with a very lovable cast of oddballs.

Rosealba’s old life now seems dull and she relishes her second chance at really living.

Bread & Tulips is a treasured, adorable film that remains well-loved many years later.

WINNER
Best Film, Best Actress, Best Actor - David di Donatello Awards
Best Director - Italian National Syndicate of Film Journalists
Best Screenplay - Italian Golden Globes

"I am not at the movies for lonely-hearts tips. I require the characters to be strange and wonderful, romantic and quirky, and above all, lovable." - Roger Ebert, Rotten Tomatoes

Romantic Comedy | Italy

Directed by Ferzan Özpetek

Diamanti

Presented by STUDIO ITALIA

Inspired by Ozpetek’s personal experience frequenting film and theatre tailoring shops in the 1980s, Diamonds features a dazzling all-star ensemble cast led by Luisa Ranieri and Jasmine Trinca, with costumes by designer Stefano Ciammitti.

In the present day, Ozpetek decides to make a film about women and so gathers his favourite actresses for a lunch and script read-through, which leads to his imagination transporting them into another era.

In 1970s Rome, sisters Alberta and Gabriella run a prestigious fashion house, where the noise of the sewing machines fills a workplace populated by women. When an important order arrives from an Oscar-winning costume designer client, challenges arise as the team of talented dressmakers try to fulfill the requirements. Outside and within the atelier, passions, anxieties, and unbreakable bonds intertwine as the line between reality and fiction begins to blur.

"A declaration of love to women, to the art of dressmaking, and the emotional power of cinema." - Vogue

Drama, Comedy | Italy | Italian with English subtitles

Directed by Giulia Louise Steigerwalt

Presented by EDIT.

In a conservative Catholic nation with draconian censorship laws, his production company was briefly a utopian dream of revolution and sexual freedom. Schicci’s venture took place in a simpler, kinder pre-internet era, but in a rapidly changing Berlusconi Italy.

Director Giulia Louise Steigerwalt paints him as a likeable impresario steering the narrative away from easy impressions. Pietro Castellitto’s acclaimed, wide-eyed performance of him as a quirky visionary whose main sin was ‘loving woemn too much’ reflects the perspective of his secretary and some of the women he worked with.

While comparisons to Boogie Nights are inevitable, the film celebrates the women’s stories, including nods to figures like Cicciolina who was famously elected as a member of the Chamber of Deputies. We are led on a lighthearted romp with unexpected wit and tenderness.

"A celebration of the golden age of an Italian prom empire." - The Hollywood Reporter

Comedy | Italy | Italian with English subtitles & English Language

Directed by Giuseppe Tornatore

Presented by The Istituto Italiano di Cultura, Sydney

After 40 years of teaching in the metropolitan jungle of Rome, primary school teacher Michele Cortese (Antonio Albanese) moves to an idyllic village in the heart of the Abruzzo National Park, population 1800, to teach at a tiny school with only a handful of students aged seven to ten. He quickly has trouble adjusting to the local culture to entertaining results but gradually adapts, thanks to the school's friendly vice-principal Agnese (Virginia Raffaele) and its spirited pupils.

However, just as all seems well, unwelcome news arrives: the school has failed to meet its student enrolment quota for the next year and will be forced to close. So begins a race against time to save it whatever it takes...

Addressing the dynamics and challenges faced by small communities - and the vital importance of educational institutions for their survival - with sensitivity and lightness, this heartwarming story won over Italian audiences, becoming the #1 local box office smash of 2024.

"Ennio Morricone, the Maestro of the movie soundtrack, gets the entrancing documentary he deserves." - Owen Gleiberman. Variety

WINNER
Best Documentary, David di Donatello Awards
Best Sound Design, David di Donatello Awards
Best Editing, David di Donatello Awards
Silver Ribbon, National Syndicate of Film Journalists
Best Documentary, Golden Globes Italy

Documentary | Italian with English subtitles

Directed by Mario Martone

Presented by Quaglia @ Casamassima

Rome, 1980.

Unable to get her novel The Art of Joy published, author Goliarda Sapienza finds herself briefly imprisoned after she steals some jewellery from a wealthy friend. The experience turns out to be life-changing, as Goliarda discovers a world without class barriers, and forms a deep bond with some of the younger inmates.

After their release and during a sweltering summer, the women continue to meet. Her friends’ stories and struggles for independence liberate Goliarda, who re-discovers the joy of living, and her drive to write.

Inspired by Sapienza’s 1983 autobiography The University of Rebibbia, Fuori is an inspiring story of friendship, female solidarity and freedom, capturing the essence of a remarkable woman ahead of her time, whose aspiration for personal and collective freedom remains topical.

"Valeria Golino shines in this tribute to maverick Italian writer Goliarda Sapienza"

In one of her finest performances to date, Golino plays the writer who found more acceptance and understanding with her fellow inmates than in Italian intellectual circles.

Drama, Biography | Italy | Italian, with English subtitles

Directed by Alessio Rigo de Righi Matteo Zoppis

Testa o Croce?

Presented by Rialto View

Set in Italy at the beginning of the 20th century when Italians were still fascinated by the myths of the Wild West.

John C. Reilly as Buffalo Bill is a likeable showman who caricatures cowboys for Italian aristocrats. Like Once Upon a Time in the West it is driven by a female protagonist, Rosa (played by French star Nadia Tereszkiewicz). Rosa falls in love with the skilful stablehand, Santino, played by Alessandro Borghi. Santino is handsome, heroic and brave and, in a comic inversion, he’s portrayed as eye candy for our heroine.

When Santino is accused of murder they on on the run. Beautiful cinematic sequences are followed by moments of unexpected magical realism. Filmed entirely on lush, celluloid film with an artful sensibility that makes the most of the stunning Italian landscapes.

"A spectacularly photographed, wittily written, romantic Western" - Carlos Aguilar, The Playlist (Cannes 2025 Review)

WINNER
Best Film, Melbourne International Film Festival
Best Directors, Tokyo International Film Festival
Jury Prize, Festival du Film Italien de Villerupt
Jury Prize, Fabrique du Cinema

Premiered
Un Certain Regard, Cannes Film Festival

Directed by Giorgia Farina

Ho Visto un Re

Presented by Brebnerprint

It’s 1936 and Mussolini’s Italy has invaded Ethiopia in its colonial fervour.

This incredible true story is set in a seaside town in a grand aristocratic estate, where young Emilio is more interested in his novels, populated with romanticised orientalist characters, than in nationalistic exploits.

His mother is an eccentric artist and his father is the overbearing, fascist mayor of the town. When a captured Ethiopian prince is imprisoned in an aviary on the family estate, Emilio imagines the exotic gentleman is a character form one of his novels. Against his father’s wishes, the two strike up a friendship.

In this clever and colourful coming-of-age film, Emilio will come to realise the true nature and absurdity of his world.

WINNER
Best Film, Pasinetti Award at the Venice Film Festival
Best Prop Maker, Venice Film Festival
Lizzani Award, Venice Film Festival

"A fable against xenophobia that deserves to be seen, discussed and appreciated." - Deadline

Directed by Ginevra Elkann

Te L’avevo Detto

Presented by PERONI

Director Ginevra Elkann has assembled a stellar cast to depict a time that may not be too far away, beyond the climate tipping point. Through a series of intertwined threads, we’re immersed in stories ranging from the hilarious to the tragic. Valeria Bruni Tedeschi plays a woman who inhabits a world of her own.

The wonderful Valeria Golino plays a botox-filled ageing porn star who pines for the spotlight but instead lives with her cats. Danny Houston plays an Amercican priest who struggles with his heroin addiction. Thse and other micro-stories create a clever mosaic of pieces that, when they come together, form a richly complex, deliciously dark comedy with outrageous poignancy.

The bold, stylised visual approach, with its hypnotic, pastel palette, is surreal, highly original and captivating.

"Brilliant and bittersweet." - Ashbury Films

Black Comedy | Italian with English subtitles

events.venue: The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington
events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Alessandro Siani

Presented by ANTHONY HARPER

A relaxed comedy that blends humour and crime and invites audiences into the chaotic lives of its two amusing leads. Alessandro Siani directs and stars as Antonio, blending a ligh-hearted romance with elements reminiscent of 1980s American buddy-cop films.

In Italy, both Siani and Pieraccioni (Pieraldo) are household names, but this is the first time they’ve appeared on screen together. It was Italy’s biggest comedy in 2024 and was shot entirely on the Adriatic Coast of Le Marche and in Ancona, giving it a laid-back seaside vibe.

It’s Time to Talk strikes a balance that keeps viewers entertained without losing sight of what makes stories compelling; human connection amid adversity, family, love, and a never-take-yourself-too-seriously attitude.

",,, a light, well-structured comedy, rich in a steady flow of gags. A comedy, yes - but in truth also a police film, a genre that always brings mystery and action."

WINNER
Best Movie, Filming Italy Award

Comedy | Italy | Italian with English subtitles

events.venue: The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington
events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Paolo Sorrentino

Presented by The Embassy of Italy, Wellington

Academy Award Winner Paolo Sorrentino possesses one of the most distinct, artful, and intelligent voices in contemporary cinema. With La Grazia, he continues to astonish audiences, but this time not only for his creative flourishes, but for an elegant, immensely thoughtful, and restrained meditation on power, morality, and legacy.

With majestic authority, Toni Servillo plays Mariano De Santis, President of the Italian Republic, in his final weeks in office. He wrestles with the legacy of his career and, for the first time, finds himself unable to make decisions. He must make a resolution on a euthanasia bill and decide whether to grant pardons for two convicted murderers. It’s in the extraordinary private and intimate sequences that we feel his grief for his now deceased wife and the scars left by her ancient infidelity.

‘La Grazia’ has the double meaning of a ‘legal pardon’ and the more spiritual significance of being in a ‘state of grace’. In La Grazia Sorrentino and his collaborator of over twenty-six years, Servillo, are indeed in a state of filmmaking grace.

"Sorrentino has made some beauties in his career. This is one of his best." - Pete Hammond. Deadline

WINNER
Best Actor, Toni Servillo, Venice Film Festival
Best Film Pasinetti Award, Venice Film Festival
Best Film Italian Film in Venice, Venice Film Festival
Best Screenplay, Chicago International Film Festival
Special Prize, Anna Ferzetti, Venice Film Festival

Drama | Italian with English subtitles

Directed by Cristiano Bortone, Daniela Porto

Il Mio Posto è Qui

Presented by GO MEDIA

In the impoverished confines of her parents’ home, 17-year-old Marta awaits the return of her fiance from war. As a single mother, she faces the scorn of her community, and in the aftermath of WWII, she finds herself promised to an older farmer.

During the village’s preparatory course for wives, she forges an unlikely friendship with Lorenzo, the village’s wedding planner.

In conservative, rural, Southern Italy, Lorenzo introduces her to a hidden community, sparking Marta’s courageous journey to challenge societal prejudices. Against the historical backdrop of the first year of women’s suffrage in Italy, Marta navigates her evolving role as a woman, breaking barriers and finding her place in a changing world.

"Female redemption that speaks to the present." - The Hollywood Reporter

WINNER
Best Directors, Bari International Film Festival
Best Screenplay, Bari International Film Festival
Best Film, Italian Film Festival Berlin
Best Film, Catalina Film Festival

events.id: IFF - Napoli - New York-The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington-Roxy Cinema
events.name: IFF - Napoli - New York
events.venue: The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington
events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Gabriele Salvatores

Presented by HOUSE OF TRAVEL & LUFTHANSA GROUP

In 1949, the Italian city of Naples lies in ruins after the devastation of WWII. Amidst the poverty and rubble-strewn streets of the city, two children, Carmine and Celestina, try to survive as best they can by helping each other. Like so many others, they dream of going to America.

After a chance encounter with a steamship’s chef, one night, they secretly stow themselves away on a ship bound for New York to reach Celestina’s sister, who emigrated to America several years earlier. On board, Carmine and Celestina join the many Italian emigrants seeking a new, better life in America.

On the run from the Italian purser (Pierfrancesco Favino), the pair eventually arrive in an unknown metropolis, which, after several misadventures, they eventually learn to call home.

The young actors live up tot he tradition of incredible performances that back to The Bicycle Thieves while Pierfrancesco Favino’s performances as the ship’s chief officer is wonderfully playful.

Salvatores celebrates, with obvious glee, many of the feel-good, sentimental and neo-realist tropes of 20th century cinema. The result is a grand film that is moving, amusing and both visually and narratively unique.

A film that can be truly enjoyed by the whole family or Italian film connoisseurs.

"A moving exploration of migration, identity, and the bittersweet search for belonging." - Natasha Senjanovic. The Hollywood Reporter

WINNER
Best Visual Effects, David di Donatello Awards
David of Youth Award
Best Score, Golden Globes Italy

Comedy, Drama | Italy | Italian with English subtitles

events.id: IFF - Once Upon a Time in the West-The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington-Roxy Cinema
events.name: IFF - Once Upon a Time in the West
events.venue: The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington
events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Sergio Leone

Presented by Illy

Charles Bronson plays the mysterious ‘man with the harmonica’ who, with outlaw Cheyenne protects the majestic Claudia Cardinale, arguably in her best role.

The standout performance comes from the wildly against-type casting of the great Henry Fonda as a ruthless assassin working for the railways. It is a film of sprawling scale, operative and exquisite in its detail, unlike an other western - cinema on a grand scale.

Sergio Leone’s collaboration with composer Ennio Morricone was one of the most creative partnerships in cinema history and its influence is still felt today. The themes are uncannily resonant today; the foundations of contemporary USA with the unstoppable force of technology and the violent, lawless brutality of unchecked greed.

This is UNMISSABLE on the big screen.

"A true masterpiece of the genre and arguable the best spaghetti western every made." - Sher Linden. The Hollywood Reporter

Spaghetti Western | Italy | Italian with English subtitles

Directed by Greta Scarano

La Vita da Grandi

Presented by Ondazzurra

Irene (Matilda De Angelis) is trying to build a regular life in Rome when she is forced to return to her hometown Rimini, to take care of Omar (newcomer Yuri Tuci), her 40-year-old autistic brother.

She will find out that Omar has very clear ideas about his future; he does not want to live with her at all when their parents are no longer around. Instead, he convinces Irene to give him an intensive course in adulthood to enable him to become independent. More importantly, he aims to fulfill his dreams, such as participating in the talent show that will make him a famous singer.

A joyous tale about overcoming obstacles and daring to go beyond the limited imposed by society and others, Siblings explores the universal bond between siblings.

OFFICIAL SELECTION
Karlovy Vary International Film Festival 2025
Bari International Film Festival

"A sensitive and soothing comedy." - Cineropa

Directed by Antonio Piazza, Fabio Grassadonia

Iddu

Presented by DELUXE | THE VAULT

In early 2000s Sicily, after serving several years in prison for Mafia-related crimes, Catello (Servillo), a long-serving local councillor, has lost everything. when the Italian Secret Service persuades him to help capture Matteo (Germano), the son of his closest friend and the last major Mafia boss still on the run, Catello sees an opportunity. A shrewd man and a tireless illusionist who turns truth into falsehood and falsehood into truth, under their guidance Catello begins to correspond with the fugitive.

Exploiting the younger man’s emotional state, Catello’s gamble involves a significant risk, as he plays a game of cat and mouse with one of the most wanted criminals in the world.

WINNER
Best Film, Pasinetti Award at the Venice Film Festival
Best Prop Maker, Venice Film Festival
Lizzani Award, Venice Film Festival

"Tony Servillo leads a ripping yarn of a mob movie." - Deadline

Italy | Drama

when the Italian Secret Service persuades him to help capture Matteo (Germano), the son of his closest friend and the last major Mafia boss still on the run, Catello sees an opportunity.
A shrewd man and a tireless illusionist who turns truth into falsehood and falsehood into truth, under their guidance Catello begins to correspond with the fugitive.
Exploiting the younger man’s emotional state, Catello’s gamble involves a significant risk, as he plays a game of cat and mouse with one of the most wanted criminals in the world.
Best Film, Pasinetti Award at the Venice Film Festival Best Prop Maker, Venice Film Festival Lizzani Award, Venice Film Festival "Tony Servillo leads a ripping yarn of a mob movie."

events.name: IFF - Somebody to Love
events.venue: The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington
events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Paolo Genovese

Follemente

Somebody to Love has swept over 2.5million moviegoers off their feet to become Italy’s #1 box office hit of 2025.

The film chronicles a first date between philosophy professor, Piero (Edoardo Leo), and talented furniture restorer, Lara Pilar Fogliati). The brilliant twist is that the film is populated by a chorus of personified emotions in their heads. A Greek chorus (or, in this case, an Italian chorus) of emotions. Over the course of the evening, they must content with competing inner motivations, instincts, logic, romance, lust, impulse, desire etc, each depicted by a hilarious cast. It’s a perfect setup for revealing the inner debates, turbulence and trepidation experienced in romance.

It is a delightful game where we’re privy to their hidden quirks, insecurities, desires and secret hopes.

A fresh, crowd-pleasing and highly entertaining new take on the comedy romance.

Can I say it? … a perfect date-night film.

"Hilarious. A comedy with a touch of class and a sense of observation of humans grappling with their emotions and postures. Unmissable." - Alvaro Moretti, Il Mesagero

Italian with English subtitles

events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Margherita Ferri

Il Ragazzo dai Pantaloni Rosa

Presented by DANTE ALIGHIERI AUCKLAND

Loosely adapted from a book by Andrea’s mother Teresa Manes (played by Claudia Pandolfi), who has since become an anti-bullying advocate, this compelling film from Margherita Ferri portrays the tragic true story of 15-year -old Andrea Spezzacatene, featuring rising star Samuele Carrino in the lead role.

Andrea is a gifted student and a talented singer who longs to make friends and fit in at his new school. but he soon falls prey to Christian, a charming student with a darker side. Then, when a laundry mishap causes his new red trousers, a gift from his mother, to turn pink in the wash, events take a turn for the worse as school bullying intensifies.

Calling attention to the impact of bullying, homophobia and intolerance, The Boy with Pink Trousers is a moving and powerful film, honouring the memory of Andrea.

"Shows the beauty and depth of the life that was lost, reminding us of the person behind the headlines." - Journey into Cinema

Family, Drama | Italian with English subtitles

events.venue: The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington
events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Andrea Segre

Berlinguer. La Grande Ambizione

Italy, 1970s. Enrico Berlinguer is the Secretary of the most important Communist Party in the western world, with over one million seven hundred thousand card-holding members and more than twelve million voters, united by the great ambition of achieving socialism within a democracy.

Challenging the dogmas of the Cold War and a world divided in two, Berlinguer and the Italian Communist Party (PCI) sought for five years to come to power, opening a season of dialogue with the Christian Democracy and almost changing history. Covering the period from 1973 when Berlinguer escapes an assassination attempt by the Bulgarian secret services in Sofia, makes it through election campaigns and trips to Moscow, onto the front pages of newspapers worldwide and holds a risky relationship with power until 1978.

The Great Ambition is a compelling portrait of the popular leaders at his peak.

"An impressive, graceful performance from Germano." - Roger Ebert

WINNER
Best Actor, Best Editing - David di Donatello Awards 2025
Best Actor - Rome Film Festival

OFFICIAL SELECTION
Goteborg Film Festival 2025 (Voyage)

Historical Drama, Biopic | Italian with English subtitles

events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Roberto Ando

Presented by SAN PELLEGRINO& FEDERAL MERCHANTS

Young idealists from all regions of Italy join Giuseppe Garibaldi in Quarto, near Genoa, for the adventure of the “Mille”. with his faithful group of officers, including the loyal Colonel Vincenzo Giodano Orsini (Servillo), Garibaldi recruits volunteers for the expedition. Among the many soldiers recruited are two (fictitious) Sicilians, peasant farmer Domenico Trico (Ficarra), and noble yet penniless trickster Rosario Spitale (Picone).

Landing at Marsala, Sicilty, the “Mille” begins fighting with the Bourbon army, whose superior numbers are immediately evident, and it seems impossible to breach enemy lines. But when is is almost forced to retreat, Garibaldi devises an ingenious plan.

Directed and co-written by Roberto Ando, this entertaining tale blends comedy and drama to illuminate a piece of history, exploring the paradoxes of Sicilian identity.

"STAGES THE PAST TO SPEAK OF THE PRESENT. ANDO DOES SO MASTERFULLY, LIGHTLY AND SHREWDLY" - Cineuropa

Drama, Comedy, Historial | Italian with English subtitles

events.id: IFF - The Last One for the Road-The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington-Roxy Cinema
events.name: IFF - The Last One for the Road
events.venue: The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington
events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Francesco Sossai

Le Città di Pianura

Presented by fish.

A story of the friendship of two fun-loving men who have never fully grown up. Born into an economic boom, but now, instead of struggling, they choose to cheerfully enjoy one tipple after another.

Doriano (Pierpaolo Capovilla) and Carlobiachi (Sergio Romano) are immensely likeable rogues who remain in a permanent state of tipsiness, yet are never creepy or tragic. Along the way, they pick up a nerdy, naive architecture student, Giulio (Filippo Scotti). Giulio soon finds himself embroiled in their escapades, but in turn conveys his appreciation for the local architecture.

Shot artfully on 35mm film, the look adds an appealing, nostalgic style that speaks to men’s age and what they’ve left behind.

I found it impossible not to love this film, and it is my indie-arthouse pick our 2026 line up.

"If you’re looking for a road-trip buddy comedy with arthouse sensibilities, Francesco Sossai has made the film for you. The Last One for the Road is one of the most charming films of the year." - Alex Papaioannou, In Session Film

WINNER
Best Actor(s) Sergio Romano, Pierpaolo Capovilla - Thessaloniki Film Festival
Best Film - Thessaloniki Film Festival

Italian with English subtitles

events.venue: The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington
events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Alvaro Longoria

Presented by BOFFI STUDIO | ELEMENTO

Millions of tourists line up to see his works in churches and museums and for centuries, counterfeits and fakes have emerged and been exposed. It seemed absolutely unthinkable that a ‘lost masterpiece’ would emerge.

In Madrid an eighty-year old woman decided to declutter and sell an old painting that had hung on her family’s walls for generations. The auction house put a EUR1500 price tag on the work and within 24 hours it was re-valued at 300million Euros. The chain of events from here is worthy of a thriller. Mysteries of provenance, government interventions between doubts about the veracity, family ructions, and fierce competitions among art dealers.

This is an extraordinary and electrifying documentary that proves that sometimes fact is stranger than fiction.

"An entertaining thriller-like documentary" - Janet Maslin. New York Times

Documentary | English, Spanish, Italian with English subtitles

Directed by Silvio Soldini

Le Assaggiatrici

Presented by Embassy of Switzerland

Autumn, 1943.

Twenty-six-year-old Rosa (Elisa Schlott) having fled Berlin, reaches the small, isolated East Prussian village of Gross-Partsch where her in-laws live and where her husband, who is on the front, has written to her to take refuge while awaiting his return.

Rosa soon discovers that the apparently peaceful village hides a secret: inside the neighbouring forest lies Hitler’s headquarters, known as Wolf’s Lair.

The Fuhrer sees enemies everywhere, and the risk of his being poisoned is his obsession.

One morning at dawn Rosa is taken, along with other young women from the village, to taste the food cooked for him. Torn between fear of death and hunger, the tasters form alliances, friendships and secret pacts among themselves, determined not to give up hope.

"Outstanding. Well shot and beautifully acted." - La Republica

WINNER
Best Screenplay, Golden Globes Italy

OFFICIAL SELECTION
Bari International Film & TV Festival

Historical Drama | Italy, Switzerland | German with English subtitles

Directed by Gabriele Fabbro

Truffles

Trifole is Presented by Sabatino

A young woman with Italian roots, Dalia, is beckoned from her home in London to visit her ailing truffle hunter grandfather, Igor (veteran screen actor Umberto Orsini). Igor now seems unable to look after himself and Dalia fears the worst. She soon discovers there’s much more to her fragile grandfather, his situation, or the bucolic landscapes than she anticipated. The breathtaking autumnal countryside and a notable great performance by the truffle dog, Birba, soon enchants and draws us into a deeper, more complex story.

It is a gentle, warm-hearted film with a few touches of the fairytale.

Trifole’s disarmingly genuine nature has connected with festival audiences worldwide.

"Trifole is the must-see film for fans of truffles, Italy and cute dogs." - Leslie Kelly, Forbes

Drama | Italian with English subtitles

events.name: IFF - Umberto Eco - A Library of the World
events.venue: The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington
events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Davide Ferrario

Presented by Istituto Italiano di Cultura, Sydney

Umberto Eco was unconventional and had a unique sense of humour, his personal library is filled with a staggeringly large collection of antique books, especially on unexpected and obscure topics. Umberto has been gone for ten years now and I feel his library was his personal legacy, a kind of metaphor for his own vast knowledge. Eco’s love for exploring anything that captured his interest is infectious; he exudes his idiosyncratic wisdom with a refreshing lightness and clarity of thought. Even if you have not read any of his books, this documentary will give you a sense of Umberto Eco’s worldwide impact as a thinker and truly captivating personality.

"A documentary about old books might sound stuff, but ‘A Library of the World’ is surprisingly fun." - POV Magazine

WINNER
Best Documentary, David di Donatello Awards
Best Sound Design, David di Donatello Awards
Best Editing, David di Donatello Awards
Silver Ribbon, National Syndicate of Film Journalists
Best Documentary, Golden Globes Italy

events.venue: The Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington
events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Alessandro Cassigoli

Presented by FARINA

Jasmine (Marilena Amato) is a Neapolitan woman whose three sons are growing older and who has always dreamed of having a daughter. Jasmine is the beating heart of the family, she runs a hairdressing business employing her son, her home life is busy and within her humble working-class family her unlikely dream causes tensions among her husband and sons.

It seems everything is against her, the bureaucracy, her finances and the lack of consensus among friends and family.

Yet, she perseveres. It feels as if we are watching a documentary, the performances are so restrained and realistic that we feel like witnesses to something truly personal, intimate and absolutely unique. It reminded me of Ken Loach’s best work.

Many of the cast are not professional actors, grounding the film in a vernacular honesty that is quietly surprising and genuinely profound.

WINNER
Fedic Award, Best Italian Film - La Biennale di Venezia
Best Italian Film, Permio Arca Cinema Giovani
Best Screenplay - Cairo International Film Festival

Drama | Italy | Italian with English subtitles

Directed by Simone Godano

10 giorni con i suoi

Fabio De Luigi and Valentina Lodovini return as Carlo and Giulia Rovelli and this time, the family is heading to sunny Puglia, where their eldest daughter, eighteen-year-old Camilla, is moving to attend university with her boyfriend, Antonio Paradiso.

However, Carlo is not ready to let go of his firstborn - especially if it means having her live with a young man he does not trust at all.

Once the Rovellis arrive at the farmhouse of the Paradiso family, Carlo does not miss an opportunity to be the world’s most unwelcome guest. Amid theft, lies, culture clashes, romantic escapades, and a series of hilarious misunderstandings, only time will tell whether the Rovellis and the Paradisos will remain at odds or become one big family.

OFFICIAL SELECTION
Italian Contemporary Film Festival 2025

"Lightheartedness and laughter for all the family" - Vanity Fair Italy

events.long_description:
Details

Directed by Fausto Brizzi

Dove osano le cicogne?

Presented by VESPA

When a devoted but wildly unprepared couple realise they are biologically unable to start a family, they hatch a plan that seems practical on paper but completely chaotic in real life - surrogacy - which is illegal in Italy.

Their decision sends them to Spain triggering a series of misunderstandings and cultural clashes. For the next nine months they must host and hide their Spanish surrogate and Marta must simulate a pregnancy hiding the truth from her old-fashioned father. Driven by sharp dialogue and a savvy sensibility, the film finds humour in bureaucracy, relationships and the absurd rules of the modern world. Beneath the laughs lies a warm, generous-hearted film directed by the comic talents of Fausto Brizzi (a well-known Italian television personality), delivering an entertaining, crowd-pleasing ride about our desire to be parents.

"A film suitable for everyone - mainstream in the truest sense of the term." - Matteo Pivetti, Sentieri Selvaggi
